title: ½ Balboa

obverse.description: Coat of arms with 9 or 10 stars above. Name of the country above, date below.
obverse.lettering:
REPUBLICA DE PANAMA
*********
PRO MUNDI BENEFICIO
2001
obverse.lettering_translation:
Republic of Panama
For the Benefit of the World

reverse.description: Armoured bust with helmet of Vasco Núñez de Balboa facing left surrounded by value in letters and wreath. The bust touches the rim below.

comments:
Balboa was a Spaniard, first European who crossed the Isthmus, reached the Pacific by land and discovered the Perlas Archipelago (1513).

The 9 stars on KM#133.1 represent the 9 provinces of the country at that time. KM#133.2 has 10 stars, as on Januari 1st, 2014 Panamá Oeste became the tenth province of Panama. From that day onward, the Coat of Arms has 10 gold stars.
From 2017 onward, 'REPUBLICA' is spelled as 'REPÚBLICA' on these coins.
Other differences between the 2001 and 2008 coins (KM#126.1) and KM#126.2:


Since its separation from Colombia in 1903, Panama has used the United States Dollar. These coins have the same specifications as the United States Half Dollar and circulate alongside it.
